status: Design recommendation and WIP source review; not final qualification

eligibilityDesign.reasonForTwoStages: The original pre-create signed configuration cannot know a future Cloud SQL createTime; never invent it or change the original config/start to retrofit it.

preflightEvidence.validUntilMs: explicit bounded expiry, no later than original cleanup horizon
preflightEvidence.effectivePermissionsEvidenceSha256: reviewed direct and inherited permissions/other automation evidence

eligibilityDesign.approvalBinding: Full signed config binds SHA256 of that complete independent report and fixed permitted identities/name. Report is source-prepared now; no genuine live proof manufactured. Avoid self-referential configDigest inside its own bound report.
deleteChecks: Validate exact signed report digest and all project/run/name/candidate/clock fields
Reject missing/expired/future/revoked/mismatched proof; retain supervised fallback
Compare durable binding to exact current ownership receipt and fresh provider GET incarnation
Any lifecycle-permission/intervention/name-registry change invalidates eligibility; absence of such changes is a future supervised verification obligation, not a live IAM claim
A valid report/config cannot add an atomic SQL DELETE precondition that the API lacks; underlying exclusive control and permanent never-reuse policy remain necessary

If independent review must cover actual post-create incarnation rather than preflight conditions plus observed ledger binding, use an explicitly separate signed cleanup attestation; never mutate original config/clock

wipFindings: Cancellation queue now precedes run LRO polling; correct direction. Direct delete_owned must enforce the same sent-run/completed-execution rule, including empty listings after lost run reply.
Stop confirmation needs durable invalidation before a new stop attempt on the same incarnation; an old confirmed operation cannot prove a later lost stop completed.
Completed execution evidence must match the tracked run sentAt/known execution, not merely an unrelated older terminal row.
After matching execution completion, a cancelled/error original run LRO must not prevent cleanup indefinitely; retain its failed outcome without requiring successful workload execution.
